newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Libya plans gas pipeline to Italy.
newsitem.headline: Libya plans gas pipeline to Italy.

text.p: Libya plans to build a pipeline to transport gas from its Atshan field to Whafa before exporting it from the Sibrata terminal to Italy, said Amin Missallati, exploration manager of Agip Oil Co Ltd. "The pipeline proposed has capacity of 15,000 to 30,000 standard cubic feet per day," Missallati told the Africa Upstream 1996 conference.

European Union officials said in August the pipeline could be hit by new U.S. legislation that punishes foreign companies that invest in oil and gas projects in Libya and Iran, which Washington alleges are involved in international terrorism.
The EU has formally protested to the U.S. concerning the legislation, saying it does not believe it to be appropriate or effective.
Missallati said Libya aims to extend its gas gathering network to recover gas currently being flared.
He said Libya recognised the importance of gas as an important future source of energy and was therefore launching comprehensive exploration and development programmes.
Through such programmes Libya aimed to increase its total gas production to three billion standard cubic feet per year by 2010 from an expected 1996 production of 1.6 billion, Missallati said.
Libya could also increase its total gas reserves to around 58 trillion cubic feet from a current 34 trillion cubic feet.
The Attahadi field had total gas reserves of 9.6 trillion cubic feet, "which will produce 300 million standard cubic feet when we go to production in the near future," he said.
The Alwafa fields had reserves totalling 2.73 trillion cubic feet and the West Half Atshan field had 1.2 trillion cubic feet, Missallati added.
Libya's total offshore and onshore gas reserves currently stand at around 34 trillion cubic feet, with possible total recovery of 16 trillion, he said.
